item.text: The engine compiles cleanly. I’m grabbing the final references now; the main result is that `Simulator` no longer owns any day/night modulo checks or weather transition timing, and the view/stats now read that same rules engine instead of inventing their own clock.

The new core is [SimulationRulesEngine.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R012_module_java/SimulationRulesEngine.java:1), with [TimeOfDay.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R012_module_java/TimeOfDay.java:1) for the day/night phase. That engine now owns the day/night cycle, periodic weather changes, manual weather overrides, and the “can this organism act on this step?” decision.

`Simulator` is correspondingly thinner. In [Simulator.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R012_module_java/Simulator.java:86) it creates the rules engine once, and in [Simulator.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R012_module_java/Simulator.java:142) it just advances rules and asks `rules.canAct(...)` instead of doing inline modulo checks. The old `randomWeather()` logic is gone. I also wired the same engine into [SimulatorView.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R012_module_java/SimulatorView.java:42) and [FieldStats.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R012_module_java/FieldStats.java:13), so the weather buttons and the population/status text now read from the same source of truth instead of duplicating clock/weather logic.
